rationale: Rollback is the optimal failure policy for hostile code autograders because untrusted student submissions frequently corrupt file systems, mutate global environment variables, and delete shared grading dependencies. Reverting to a clean microVM snapshot guarantees deterministic idempotency, eliminates inter-test contamination, ensures strict grading fairness across runs, and prevents resource leaks without incurring the cold-boot latency of creating brand new VM instances.
